question.problem: Find the derivative of the function $y = x^{x^3}.$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y = x^{x^3}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{{x}^{3}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & ={x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =({x}^{3})^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+({x}^{3})\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =3{x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x+{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $y'{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=x^{x^3}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & ={x}^{{x}^{3}}(3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+{x}^{2}) \\  & ={x}^{{x}^{3}}({x}^{2}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)) \\  & ={x}^{{x}^{3}+2}(3\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)\end{aligned}
$$
